factProposals.value: An integrations and readiness screen in the staff console showing each external connection (City GIS, Blue Stakes, Madison AI, Lama, SpryPoint) with its status and last successful call, and each go-live readiness check with pass or fail and its evidence.
Connection status is read from the call logs the integrations already write: the GIS call log, the Blue Stakes call log and the vendor feed log, plus on-demand checks of GIS.
A new append-only record of on-demand integration checks: who asked, when, and the outcome (ok, unexpected_payload, error, timeout or unauthorized). It holds call results, never a status.
Project managers and administrators (readiness:review) see the view and run checks; field crew are refused and the refusal is recorded.

A connection that has never been called shows no last successful call; a failing one shows its error class and the time it began failing; a reply that succeeds with an unexpected shape is a failure; a readiness item marked done with no note shows as no evidence recorded.

decisions.statement: Work out every connection status from the call records on each request instead of storing a status.
decisions.rationale: A stored flag can be left behind after a failure; a status computed from the latest real call cannot.
decisions.evidence: server/integrationStatus.js; tests/integrationStatus.test.js (the status follows the latest real call)

decisions.statement: Check now makes a read-only GIS call (changes since the sync position, without moving it) through the existing GIS client.
decisions.rationale: It must be a real call with the same timeout, capped retries and logging as every other GIS call, and running it twice must change nothing.

decisions.statement: Treat the vendor connections as one-way: their status comes from their requests to our feed, and a feed answer that breaks the vendor contract is shown as a mismatch.
decisions.rationale: We have no vendor endpoints or credentials to call; vendors read from us.

limitations.statement: Only GIS can be checked on demand. Blue Stakes has no read-only call, and the vendors are not called by the system, so their status comes from their real calls only.
GIS and Blue Stakes are stand-ins in this build, and the screen says so; no live service has been connected.

The prompt's failure path 'a vendor endpoint returns success with an unexpected payload shape' assumes the system calls vendor endpoints; it does not, so it is met for GIS replies and for vendor contract mismatches instead.
